distinct_answers.text: Thin. Job 16:9 (sa.tam) attributes hatred/grudge-bearing to God in a lament context ("he has torn me in his wrath and hated me; he has gnashed his teeth at me; my adversary sharpens his eyes against me") — Job's language moves between human and divine adversary, and the adversary figure is significant. Within the M06-A evidence itself, no verse explicitly names a spiritual being other than God as the subject of hatred.
No evidence of contempt, abhorrence, cruelty, reproach, or malice operating in relation to angelic or adversarial spiritual beings in these sub-groups.

Yes — the most significant finding for the cluster. 1Pe 5:8: "your adversary the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour." The adversary relationship explicitly names the devil as the cosmic antidikos. This is the only verse in the entire M06 cluster that names an adversarial spiritual being as the active agent of a characteristic. The inner-being response commanded is sober watchfulness and firm resistance in faith — the same structural response as in the human-legal adversary context, but with the cosmic dimension added.
[Sub-group not separately addressed in source — see cluster-level finding (cluster_subgroup_id IS NULL) for this prompt]
The other sub-groups are silent on adversarial spiritual being engagement in their primary verse evidence.

Yes — uniquely and in a negative register. 1Cor 10:20 (Group 1057): "I do not want you to be participants with demons" — koinōnos with demons is explicitly named as a possibility to be avoided. This is the only verse in M05 that explicitly names an adversarial spiritual being as a koinōnos of the human person.

The adversarial spiritual beings interface is evidenced only in M05-G, and exclusively in the negative register. The fellowship characteristic is the most spiritually dangerous in M05 — it names the possibility of participation with demonic powers (through idol worship) alongside the highest form of participation (in the divine nature — 2Pe 1:4 — Group 1057). The range of M05-G's koinōnos is from the lowest (participation with demons) to the highest (participation in divine nature) — the widest spiritual register of any characteristic in M05.

**[A1 — God Righteousness]** Yes — the heavens declare God's righteousness (Psa 50:6; 97:6, VSG M26-A1-005). The angelic/heavenly realm is involved in the proclamation of God's righteousness. Christ is "vindicated by the Spirit" (1Ti 3:16, VSG 3194-001) — a spiritual-being interface at the moment of Christ's vindication.

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Yes — Heb 11:7 (VSG 4846-001): "by faith Noah... constructed an ark for the saving of his household. By this he condemned the world and became an heir of the righteousness that comes by faith." The context implies the larger cosmic witness — Noah's righteous act condemned the world (a spiritual-judicial act with cosmic scope).

**[D — Avenging Justice]** Yes — Rev 6:10 (VSG 944-001): the martyrs under the altar cry out to God for justice. The heavenly-judicial setting places the cry for avenging justice in direct interface with the divine-heavenly realm.
**[E — Condemnation]** No direct spiritual-beings interface evidenced for condemnation beyond the divine interface already covered in T4.1.
**[F — Moral Reckoning]** No spiritual-beings interface evidenced.
**[G — Structural Opposites]** The adversarial spiritual dimension is not directly evidenced in the G verse evidence for M26. Silence.

**[CLUSTER — T4.6]** E. The spiritual beings interface in M26 is primarily mediated through: (1) the heavenly declaration of God's righteousness (A1-005); (2) the martyrs' cry for justice in the heavenly court (D: Rev 6:10); and (3) Christ's vindication by the Spirit (C-adjacent: 1Ti 3:16). The spiritual beings interface is present but not a dominant theme — the primary interfaces are God-to-human and human-to-human.

VCG01 (Jas 3:15-17): wisdom from above vs earthly-natural-demonic wisdom — the adversarial being's wisdom as the alternative to divine wisdom. VCG02 (1Ki 3:12): divine giving of wisdom as the background against which adversarial operations are implicitly opposed.
VCG04 (M15-B — judicial withholding): God closing understanding. VCG06 (Luk 24:45): Christ opening understanding — both divine positive and negative operations on the perceptive faculty.
VCG07 (Gen 3): the serpent's role in offering knowledge of good and evil — adversarial transmission of moral knowing. VCG01 (Psa 139:6): God's comprehensive knowing.
VCG07 (2Cor 10:4): strongholds and arguments include spiritually-adversarial cognitive structures.
VCG03 (Isa 14:24-27): the irresistible divine purpose operating over against human and adversarial counsel.

VCG02 (Matt 1:20): the angel intervenes in Joseph's meditative state — spiritual beings operate in the meditative-reflective space. VCG04 (Amos 4:13): God declaring what is in the creature's inner reflection.
VCG01 (2Cor 4:4): the god of this age blinds the noēmata — the clearest instance of adversarial spiritual engagement with an inner faculty in the cluster.
VCG01 (Eph 6:17 corpus): the word of God as the sword of the Spirit — weaponry in spiritual warfare. VCG01 (1Cor 1:18): the logos operates in the domain of spiritual contestation.
Jude 9 is the defining verse: angelic-adversarial disputation — Michael and the devil in direct contestation. The mode is reasoned disputation (dialegō), not force.

None of the M20 terms are explicitly linked to adversarial spiritual activity in the verse evidence. The cluster's 57 verses contain no explicit reference to demonic or angelic engagement with these characteristics.

Partial. H2604 cha.nan group 989-001 (Dan 6:11): "Daniel making petition and plea before his God" — the context of Daniel's sustained grace-petition occurs amid adversarial political opposition (Dan 6 is the lion's den narrative). The grace-petition sustains Daniel through the adversarial environment. Act 27:24 (5470-001): "God has granted you all those who sail with you" — this occurs in a crisis context, but no spiritual being is explicitly named. No verse in M39-A names angelic involvement in the grace dynamic directly.
No verse in M39-B explicitly names angelic or adversarial spiritual beings in relation to the goodness characteristic.

The most significant spiritual-beings interface in M46-A is Rev 3:17-18: the Risen Christ addressing the Laodicean church with the diagnosis of their inner closure and the counsel for its remedy. This is not the human realm but the risen Lord's direct address to the inner-closed community. The letter addresses the wealth-domain spiritual condition.

Rev 18 (Babylon's wealth-system) has an implicit spiritual-beings dimension: Babylon is described in terms that suggest it is not merely an economic system but a spiritual power (Rev 17:5 — "Mystery, Babylon the Great"). The merchants who grew rich from Babylon's wealth were participating in a spiritual-economic system. The judgement of Babylon is a spiritual-warfare event.
No direct spiritual-beings interface evidenced in M46-C or M46-D beyond the divine interface already addressed in T4.1.

M01-A shows fear of God operating in the angelic realm: Psa 89:7 (God is "greatly to be feared among the holy ones in the divine council — his awesomeness surpasses all heavenly beings, making reverential fear the only fitting inner response **even in heaven**"). Fear of God is not merely a human posture but the appropriate posture of the divine council before God. Gen 22:12 (the angel of the Lord affirming Abraham's fear of God as evidenced by his willingness to sacrifice — the fear tested and confirmed through angelic mediation).

M01-B shows angelic mediation of fear extensively: the angelic appearances throughout the NT that produce fear in human persons (Luk 1:12-13; Luk 2:9-10; Mat 28:4-5; Luk 24:5; Act 10:4; Rev 1:17) are the most concentrated evidence. Angels both produce acute fear and command its release ("do not be afraid" from angels across the corpus). Angels operate as the interface through which divine holiness makes itself felt in the human inner life.

M01-B-VCG-01 (fear before supernatural encounters) shows specific instances of adversarial encounter producing fear: Dan 7:7 (the fourth beast — terrifying in appearance, producing fear — in the visionary realm); Mar 14:33 (Jesus in Gethsemane, ekthambeo — though this is the suffering Son before the Father's judgment rather than adversarial encounter). The adversarial spiritual dimension is present but not dominant in the evidenced material.

M01-F-VCG-04's fearful expectation of judgment (Heb 10:27) operates in the context of divine judgment as the eschatological reality — a spiritual-being interface in the sense that it anticipates encountering God as judge.

Angelic beings are prominent mediators of M01-B fear (appearances producing fear, commands releasing fear). The divine council evidences reverential fear of God (Psa 89:7 — M01-A). Adversarial spiritual operations are less prominent in the evidenced material: the beasts of Daniel's visions (M01-B-VCG-01) and the general spiritual-resistance context of M01-G (Rev 21:8's apostasy-under-pressure) are the nearest instances.

Yes. Rev 12:17 (M02-B-VCG-02): "the dragon's fury is a specific inner reaction to being thwarted by the woman; it drives him outward into active warfare against her offspring." Spiritual beings (the dragon/adversary) experience and act from anger. The characteristic is not exclusively human or divine — it is operative in adversarial spiritual beings.

Rev 11:18 (M02-A-VCG-02): "God's wrath arrives as a decisive, timed response to the nations' own raging" — the nations' rage (which may include demonic spiritual influence, per the Revelation context) is the occasion for divine wrath's arrival. The characteristic operates across the spiritual-beings interface as both a spiritual-beings state (dragon's fury) and a response to spiritual-beings activity (God's wrath responding to collective human-spiritual rage).

Two instances of spiritual beings and grief. In M03-BOUNDARY, the demonic fear of torment (Mat 8:29; Mar 5:7; Luk 8:28 — G0928G basanizō BOUNDARY) shows spiritual beings in relation to a form of anguish/torment — but this is demonic beings dreading suffering imposed by divine authority, not human-person grief. In M03-E-VCG-02, the Spirit intercedes within the believer's spirit with groanings too deep for words (Rom 8:26) — the Spirit participates in the groaning of the believer, showing a divine-spiritual being sharing in and expressing grief alongside the human person.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The evidence does not name angelic beings as participants in exultation in this corpus. The cosmic rejoicing passages (Psa 96:11; 97:1; 1Ch 16:31) include the heavens and earth but do not specify angelic beings. The inverted passages (Pro 2:14; Hos 10:5; Hos 9:1) show the characteristic distorted by idolatrous and demonic influence (idols as the displaced objects of exultation) but do not name spiritual adversaries directly.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes. (1) **Heavenly/angelic Joy** — Luk 15:7 ("joy in heaven over one sinner who repents"); Luk 15:10 ("joy before the angels of God") — Joy is an active reality in the heavenly realm, responsive to human repentance; (2) **The Holy Spirit as Joy-agent** — Gal 5:22; 1Th 1:6; Rom 14:17; Act 13:52 — the Spirit is the agent of Joy in the NT's Spirit-mediated register; Luk 10:21 (Jesus rejoices "in the Holy Spirit") — the Spirit is the medium of Christ's own Joy; (3) **Eschatological angelic context** — Jude 24 ("with great joy" before God's presence — at the final presentation); Rev 4:9; 7:12 (heavenly creatures giving thanks — the joy-adjacent thanksgiving of heavenly worship).

**[CHAR-7]** E — Yes: (1) **The Holy Spirit as producer** — Luk 10:21; 1Th 1:6; Act 13:52 — the Spirit is the primary agent of Suffering-Joy's most intense form; the characteristic is directly Spirit-mediated; (2) **Angelic context** — Luk 1:44 (the baby leaping at Mary's Spirit-anointed greeting — the Spirit who has overshadowed Mary transmits through the incarnation-announcement context); Mat 5:12's "reward in heaven" implies the angelic-heavenly realm as the context within which the reward awaits.

**[CHAR-3]** S — The evidence does not show Gladness operating in relation to angelic or adversarial spiritual beings in the M04-L or M04-O corpus. Neh 9:20's "good Spirit to instruct them" attributes goodness to the divine Spirit but does not show the Spirit as an agent of Gladness transmission in the M04 sense. No angelic or adversarial interface is evidenced.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes: (1) **The beast-captivation** (M04-N-VCG-02; Rev 13:3; 17:8) — the most explicit spiritual-beings interface in the corpus: the beast (an adversarial spiritual power) is the object of the whole earth's marveling-Delight; the characteristic of Delight is here shown as the instrument through which an adversarial spiritual power captivates the unredeemed; (2) **Idol-worship Delight** (M04-P-VCG-01; Eze 6:13; 16:19; 20:28) — Israel's ni.cho.ach directed toward idols; the pleasing-aroma of worship diverted from YHWH to spiritual powers with demonic associations (the "gods" of the nations); (3) **Wisdom's delight** (Pro 8:30–31) — Personified Wisdom (widely read in Jewish tradition as a created being or divine attribute personified) as the object of divine Delight before creation.

**[CHAR-5]** S — The M04-J and M04-K corpus does not explicitly show Pleasure operating in relation to angelic beings. The ni.cho.ach aroma reaches God and is received by him; angels are not named as participants. The Psa 36:8 "river of delights" and Psa 16:11 "pleasures forevermore" are in God's presence, but the angelic dimension is not named.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Yes: (1) **Heavenly assembly** — Psa 89:5 ("let the heavens praise your wonders, O Lord, your faithfulness in the assembly of the holy ones") — Wonder is the appropriate response of the holy ones (angelic beings) to God's extraordinary works; (2) **Dark Wonder at adversarial powers** — Dan 8:24 ("fearful destruction"); Dan 11:36 (astonishing blasphemy) — the adversarial king whose acts produce dark wonder; (3) **Unclean spirits** — Mar 1:27 (thambeō arising from the exorcism of an unclean spirit — the crowd's Wonder at Jesus' authority over spiritual powers); (4) **The angel questioning Wonder** — Rev 17:7 (the angel addressing John's marvelling at the harlot) — an angelic being redirecting misapplied human Wonder.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Spiritual being interfaces vary significantly across the seven: (1) **Most directly Spirit-constituted**: Suffering-Joy (Char 7) — the Holy Spirit is the primary producing agent (Luk 10:21; 1Th 1:6); Joy (Char 2) — the Spirit is the agent of Joy in its most intense forms (Gal 5:22; Act 13:52); (2) **Angelic announcement**: Joy (Char 2) — Luk 2:10 (angel announces "good news of great joy"); Luk 1:14 (Gabriel announces Zechariah's Joy); (3) **Heavenly assembly**: Wonder (Char 6) — Psa 89:5 (the holy ones praised God's wonders); Joy (Char 2) — Luk 15:7, 10 (joy before the angels over repentance); (4) **Adversarial exploitation**: Delight (Char 4) — the most directly exploited characteristic; beast-captivation (Rev 13:3; 17:8) and idol-worship ni.cho.ach (M04-P-VCG-01) both show adversarial powers redirecting the Delight faculty; Wonder (Char 6) — adversarial generation of dark-wonder blasphemy (Dan 11:36); misdirected John's marvelling (Rev 17:6–7); (5) **Silently evidenced**: Gladness (Char 3) — no angelic or adversarial interface; Pleasure (Char 5) — adversarial exploitation of Pleasure through deceptive appearances (Pro 9:17; 7:18) is implicit but not named; Exultation (Char 1) — the idolatrous-exultation passages imply adversarial misdirection without naming spiritual beings.

**[CHAR-1]** S — The 224-verse CHAR-1 corpus does not directly evidence shame operating in the person's relation to angelic or adversarial spiritual beings. The evidence is centred on the human-God and human-human axes.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Limited but present. Mar 1:25 (vc=30400) — Jesus silencing the demon — is CHAR-2 applied to an adversarial spiritual being: the demon's voice and presence are forcibly suppressed. Mar 4:39 (vc=30401) — the storm muzzled — applies the same authority to natural forces. These confirm the enforced-abasement mechanism applies beyond human persons when divine authority acts against them.

The world's contempt structures may be demonically energised (the parable of the tenants who reject the son could carry this dimension), but the text does not name this explicitly. Silent.

**[CHAR-6]** S — The 8-verse CHAR-6 corpus does not evidence innocence-as-counter-to-shame operating in relation to angelic or adversarial spiritual beings. Silent.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Limited but present. Char 2 provides the primary evidence: Jesus silencing the demon (Mar 1:25) and the storm (Mar 4:39) as applications of the enforced-abasement mechanism to spiritual and natural forces. Beyond this, the cluster is substantially silent on the spiritual beings interface — M07's primary field is the human-to-human and human-to-God relational space. The one significant interpretive observation: the enemy-language of Char 1's M07-A unjust-wound register (Psa 25:2-3; 35:4-5; 129:5) acknowledges enemies as the agents of unjust shame; whether these enemies carry an adversarial spiritual dimension is not named explicitly in the corpus, though the lament psalms' enemy-language could carry this dimension. Classified as silent on the specific spiritual beings interface pending further investigation.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Partially. Dan 11:36 (vc=34235, M08-A1-VCG-02): "the king shall do as he wills. He shall exalt himself and magnify himself above every god" — CHAR-1 explicitly directed against the divine order, extending beyond any single deity to claim supremacy over "every god." Isa 14:13 (vc=34233, M08-A4-VCG-05): "I will ascend to heaven; above the stars of God I will set my throne on high" — the will's self-elevation into the heavenly domain, claiming ascendancy above the heavenly order. 2Ki 19:22 (vc=34160, vc=65755, M08-A4-VCG-05) and Isa 37:23 (vc=34304, M08-A4-VCG-05): the Assyrian king's pride directed against "the Holy One of Israel" with eyes lifted to the heights and voice raised — CHAR-1 operating as defiance directed against the divine person specifically. These verses evidence CHAR-1 in the vertical-against-God direction but do not directly address other spiritual beings (angelic or adversarial) as distinct from God.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes. 2Pe 2:10 (vc=4670, vc=42739, M08-B-VCG-03): "the bold man [tolmētēs]... bold in blasphemy" and "self-willed, they do not tremble before the glorious ones" — CHAR-2 directed against spiritual beings designated as "glorious ones." This is the most direct evidence in the 45-verse corpus of CHAR-2 operating in the spiritual-beings interface. The "glorious ones" (whether angelic beings or other spiritual authorities) are the specific object of CHAR-2's self-willed refusal to tremble — the reckless boldness of tolmētēs is directed precisely at what should command reverence.

**[CHAR-3]** S — The verse evidence in §3.B does not evidence CHAR-3 operating in relation to angelic or adversarial spiritual beings specifically. The spiritual reference points in VCG-03 are God/Christ/Spirit as the objects of God-directed boasting (Phili 3:3: worship by the Spirit; 1Cor 1:31: boast in the Lord) rather than other spiritual beings.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes — through the adversarial paradigm reference. 1Ti 3:6 (vc=33924, M08-D-VCG-02): "he may become puffed up with conceit and fall into the condemnation of the devil" — the devil is explicitly invoked as the paradigm case of CHAR-4's judgment. This is the most direct connection between a human inner-being characteristic and adversarial spiritual activity in M08: CHAR-4's conceited cognitive self-inflation replicates the adversarial paradigm and receives the same condemnation.

**[CHAR-5]** S — The verse evidence in §3.D does not directly evidence CHAR-5 operating in relation to angelic or adversarial spiritual beings. The characteristic operates in the human structural-power register.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster comparison surfaces two significant spiritual-beings connections. CHAR-2: 2Pe 2:10 (M08-B-VCG-03) — CHAR-2 directed against "glorious ones" (angelic/spiritual authorities) through the tolmētēs (reckless boldness). CHAR-4: 1Ti 3:6 (M08-D-VCG-02) — human CHAR-4 connected to "the condemnation of the devil" — the adversarial paradigm case of cognitive self-inflation. CHAR-1: Dan 11:36 (M08-A1-VCG-02) — "magnifying himself above every god" — CHAR-1 directed against the divine order including its spiritual-beings dimension. CHAR-3 and CHAR-5 are silent on spiritual-beings interface. The cluster-synthesis: M08's spiritual-beings interface is concentrated in CHAR-2 (directed against angelic authorities) and CHAR-4 (connected to the adversarial paradigm case). CHAR-4's 1Ti 3:6 connection is the cluster's most theologically significant spiritual-beings finding.

**[CHAR-2]** S — The Submission corpus does not directly evidence the characteristic operating in relation to angelic or adversarial spiritual beings. The characteristic's relational structure in the evidence is constitutively human-to-divine and human-to-human.

**[CHAR-3]** S — The two-verse corpus does not directly evidence the characteristic operating in relation to angelic or adversarial spiritual beings. The relational structure in both verses is exclusively divine-human.
**[CHAR-4]** S — The two-verse corpus does not evidence the characteristic operating in relation to angelic or adversarial spiritual beings.
**[CHAR-5]** S — The three-verse corpus does not evidence the characteristic operating in relation to angelic or adversarial spiritual beings.
**[CHAR-6]** S — The five-verse corpus does not evidence the characteristic operating in relation to angelic or adversarial spiritual beings.

**[CHAR-1]** S — The Humility corpus does not directly evidence the characteristic operating in relation to angelic or adversarial spiritual beings. The characteristic's relational structure in the evidence is God-ward and human-ward.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Only CHAR-1 Humility has evidenced spiritual-beings engagement, and it is through distortion rather than direct operation: Col2:18 — the false humility involving "worship of angels" — the characteristic's site (humility) is occupied by a counterfeit that incorporates adversarial spiritual activity. The other five characteristics are silent on spiritual-beings interface. Cluster-level: M09 is not a spiritual-warfare cluster in the explicit sense — the cluster's primary spiritual engagement is through the conscience, the will, and the divine-human relational structure rather than through named adversarial spiritual powers. The one indirect adversarial evidence (Col2:18 false-humility involving angel-worship) confirms that where M09 characteristics can be distorted, the distortion may involve spiritually adversarial dynamics — but this is the exception rather than the cluster's dominant register.

## T5 — Transformation and Formation

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes. 2Pe 2:4 provides direct evidence: "God did not spare angels when they sinned, but cast them into hell and committed them to chains of gloomy darkness to be kept until the judgment." Angels committed wilful sinning — the same characteristic (cha.ta/hamartanō) that the human corpus addresses. Their sinning resulted in immediate divine judgment and permanent imprisonment. The angels are thus participants in wilful sinning, not merely observers or tempters. Additionally, the Eze 28:16 cherub passage ("you sinned; so I cast you as a profane thing from the mountain of God") evidences a guardian cherub's sinning — a spiritual being of high standing whose sinning produced expulsion from God's presence.

**[CHAR-10]** S — The 5-verse corpus contains no direct evidence of these mechanisms operating in relation to angelic or adversarial spiritual beings. The mechanisms operate in human relational contexts (enticers and the enticed, hypocritical community, accusers of Paul).

**[CHAR-11]** E — Yes. Act 26:18 — "from the power of Satan to God" — the condition places the person within Satan's power-domain; the condition's location is in the domain of the adversarial spiritual power. Gal 1:4 — "deliver us from the present evil age" — the condition is part of the "present evil age" that has a spiritual-power dimension. Eph 2:1 — "dead in trespasses and sins" is followed (in the broader Eph 2:2 context — not in the 5-verse corpus but structurally implied) by the reference to the prince of the power of the air; the condition's domain involves the adversarial spiritual power.

**[CHAR-12]** E — Yes — the adversarial spiritual dimension is explicitly named. 1Jo 3:8 — "whoever makes a practice of sinning is of the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the beginning" — the devil is the originary sinning-power whose domain the enslaved person enters through practice; sin's enslaving power is directly connected to the devil's primordial sinning identity. 1Jo 5:18 — "the evil one does not touch him" — the evil one is the specific spiritual agent through whom sin's enslaving power seeks to regain the born-of-God person; the liberation is specifically described as protection from the evil one's touch.

**[CHAR-13]** S — The 205-verse corpus does not explicitly connect the divine record to spiritual beings (angels or adversarial powers). The record operates between the human person and God directly; no angelic or adversarial spiritual agent is explicitly named as a mediator of the record in this corpus. The characteristic is constitutively a human-divine transaction.

**[CHAR-14]** S — The 34-verse corpus does not explicitly name spiritual beings (angelic or adversarial) in connection with forgiveness sought and received. The characteristic operates directly between the human person and God through the priestly or Christological mechanism.

**[CHAR-15]** S — The 8-verse corpus does not explicitly name spiritual beings (angelic or adversarial) in connection with generational sin. The condition operates within the human-God covenant relationship without named spiritual-beings mediation.

**[CHAR-16]** E — Yes — through the angelic joy dimension. Luk 15:10 — "there is joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents" — the angels are the witnesses of the sinner's repentance; their joy is the spiritual-beings' response to the sinner-identity's reversal. The angels' rejoicing names the sinner-repentance as a spiritually cosmic event, not merely a human-scale moral turning.

**[CHAR-17]** S — The 97-verse corpus does not explicitly name spiritual beings (angelic or adversarial) in connection with guilt as inner-being state. The one near-exception is Isa 6:7 — the seraph touches Isaiah's lips and removes his guilt — but this is divine agent (seraph as God's messenger) acting on God's behalf, not an independent spiritual being mediating guilt.

**[CHAR-18]** S — The 162-verse corpus does not explicitly name angelic or adversarial spiritual beings in connection with iniquity-as-accumulated-moral-crime as its primary agent. The characteristic operates within the direct human-God moral relationship. The seraph in Isa 6:7 (touching Isaiah's lips to remove guilt) is the nearest instance, but this falls in CHAR-17's removal dimension; the CHAR-18 iniquity-accumulation corpus does not feature named spiritual beings mediating its accumulation or maintenance.

**[CHAR-19]** E — Yes — through the Isa 53:12 servant-intercession passage and the Heb 2:2 angelic-law passage. Isa 53:12 — "he was numbered with the transgressors; yet he bore the sin of many, and makes intercession for the transgressors" — the servant (who is both human and divine agent) intercedes among the transgressors; this intercession is directed toward God on behalf of human transgressors. Heb 2:2 — "the message declared by angels proved to be reliable, and every transgression or disobedience received a just retribution" — angels are named as the mediators of the law whose reliability undergirds the transgression-retribution principle.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes. Num 22:34 is the primary spiritual-beings evidence: Balaam's inadvertent sinning occurred in the context of the angel of the Lord standing in the road against him — a fact hidden from Balaam until the angel was made visible. The spiritual being (angel of the Lord) was the morally relevant fact that Balaam's perception did not register, producing the inadvertent violation. The angel's disclosure is what transforms Balaam's uninformed violation into a consciously acknowledged sin requiring confession and offered reversal. The spiritual being operates as the *disclosure agent* — the one who surfaces the morally relevant truth that the inadvertent sinner did not perceive.

**[CHAR-20]** S — The 101-verse corpus does not explicitly name angelic or adversarial spiritual beings in connection with faithlessness as covenant-breaking sin. The characteristic operates within the direct human-God and human-human covenantal relationship without named spiritual-being mediation.

**[CHAR-21]** E — Yes — through the serpent-type passage. 2Cor 11:3 — "as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, your thoughts will be led astray" — the serpent is named as the archetypal external corrupting agent; the serpent's deceptive cunning is the model for the false teachers' thought-corrupting strategy. The serpent-type names an adversarial spiritual agency as the paradigmatic external source of the perversion of thought.

**[CHAR-22]** S — The 72-verse corpus does not explicitly name angelic or adversarial spiritual beings in connection with injustice as moral failure of right conduct. The characteristic operates within the direct human-God and human-human relational framework without named spiritual-being mediation.

**[CHAR-3]** S — The CHAR-3 corpus contains no direct evidence of confession operating in relation to angelic or adversarial spiritual beings. All confessions in the corpus are directed toward God, human persons, or community.

**[CHAR-4]** S — The 8-verse corpus contains no direct evidence of conscience suppression operating in relation to angelic or adversarial spiritual beings. All instances are human conditions addressed by divine or human moral authority (prophets, apostles).

**[CHAR-5]** S — The 18-verse corpus contains no direct evidence of refusal to repent operating in relation to angelic or adversarial spiritual beings. The characteristic is presented throughout as a human-to-God relational phenomenon without spiritual-being interface.

**[CHAR-6]** S — The 14-verse corpus contains no direct evidence of habitual defection operating in relation to angelic or adversarial spiritual beings. 2Ki 17:7's "feared other gods" may imply spiritual dimensions behind the false gods, but the verse names the inner human disposition (fearing) and the objects (other gods) without engaging the spiritual-being interface directly.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Limited but present.
